stem: Write the first two terms of the sequence whose nth term is \(t_n = 3n - 4\).
solution: Substituting in \(t_n = 3n - 4\): \(t_1 = 3(1) - 4 = -1\) and \(t_2 = 3(2) - 4 = 2\). Hence the first two terms are \(-1\) and \(2\).

stem: Find the value of \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) in the following quadratic equation: \(2x^2 - x - 3 = 0\).
solution: Comparing \(2x^2 - x - 3 = 0\) with the general form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), we get \(a = 2\), \(b = -1\) and \(c = -3\).

stem: Write the quadratic equation whose roots are \(-2\) and \(-3\).
solution: Let the roots be \(\alpha = -2\) and \(\beta = -3\). Then \(\alpha + \beta = -5\) and \(\alpha\beta = 6\). The required equation is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\), i.e. \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0\).

stem: Find the value of determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\).
solution: \(\begin{vmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = (4 \times 1) - (-2 \times 3) = 4 + 6 = 10\).

stem: Write the sample space for selecting a day randomly of the week.
solution: The sample space is \(S = \{\text{Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday}\}\), so \(n(S) = 7\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: Find the class mark of the classes 20-30 and 30-40.
solution: Class mark \(= \dfrac{\text{lower limit} + \text{upper limit}}{2}\). For 20-30: \(\dfrac{20 + 30}{2} = 25\). For 30-40: \(\dfrac{30 + 40}{2} = 35\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
Below is the given frequency distribution of words in an essay. Find the mean number of words written.

| Number of Words | Number of Candidates |
|---|---|
| 600 - 800 | 8 |
| 800 - 1000 | 22 |
| 1000 - 1200 | 40 |
| 1200 - 1400 | 18 |
| 1400 - 1600 | 12 |
solution: Class marks \(x_i\): \(700, 900, 1100, 1300, 1500\). Then \(f_i x_i\): \(5600, 19800, 44000, 23400, 18000\), giving \(\sum f_i = 100\) and \(\sum f_i x_i = 110800\). Mean \(= \dfrac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i} = \dfrac{110800}{100} = 1108\). The mean number of words written is \(1108\).

stem:
Subjectwise marks obtained by a student in an examination are given below. Draw pie diagram.

| Subject | Marks |
|---|---|
| Marathi | 85 |
| Hindi | 85 |
| Science | 90 |
| Mathematics | 100 |
| Total | 360 |
solution: Central angle for a subject \(= \dfrac{\text{marks}}{360} \times 360^\circ\). Marathi \(= \dfrac{85}{360} \times 360^\circ = 85^\circ\), Hindi \(= 85^\circ\), Science \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ\), Mathematics \(= \dfrac{100}{360} \times 360^\circ = 100^\circ\) (total \(360^\circ\)). Draw a circle and mark four sectors with these central angles, labelling each subject.

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by using formula method: \(5m^2 + 5m - 1 = 0\).
solution: Here \(a = 5\), \(b = 5\), \(c = -1\). \(m = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{-5 \pm \sqrt{25 + 20}}{10} = \dfrac{-5 \pm \sqrt{45}}{10} = \dfrac{-5 \pm 3\sqrt{5}}{10}\). The roots are \(\dfrac{-5 + 3\sqrt{5}}{10}\) and \(\dfrac{-5 - 3\sqrt{5}}{10}\).

stem:
There are three boys and two girls. A committee of two is to be formed. Find the probability of the following events:
Event A: The committee contains at least one girl.
Event B: The committee contains one boy and one girl.
solution: With boys \(B_1, B_2, B_3\) and girls \(G_1, G_2\), the sample space of two-member committees is \(S = \{B_1B_2, B_1B_3, B_2B_3, B_1G_1, B_1G_2, B_2G_1, B_2G_2, B_3G_1, B_3G_2, G_1G_2\}\), so \(n(S) = 10\). Event A (at least one girl): \(n(A) = 7\), so \(P(A) = \dfrac{7}{10}\). Event B (one boy and one girl): \(n(B) = 6\), so \(P(B) = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}\).

The marks scored by students in Mathematics in a certain Examination are given below. Draw histogram for the above data.

| Marks Scored | Number of Students |
|---|---|
| 0 - 20 | 3 |
| 20 - 40 | 8 |
| 40 - 60 | 19 |
| 60 - 80 | 18 |
| 80 - 100 | 6 |
solution: Take the class intervals \(0\text{-}20, 20\text{-}40, 40\text{-}60, 60\text{-}80, 80\text{-}100\) (marks) on the X-axis and the number of students on the Y-axis. Draw adjacent rectangles of heights \(3, 8, 19, 18, 6\) over the respective class intervals to obtain the histogram.

| 20 - 25 | 2 |
| 25 - 30 | 5 |
| 30 - 35 | 8 |
| 35 - 40 | 12 |

solution: Compute class marks: \(22.5, 27.5, 32.5, 37.5, 42.5, 47.5\) with frequencies \(2, 5, 8, 12, 10, 7\). Add the class marks \(17.5\) and \(52.5\) with frequency \(0\) at the two ends. Plot the points (class mark, frequency) and join them with line segments to form the frequency polygon.

Solve the following simultaneous equations:
\(\dfrac{7}{2x + 1} + \dfrac{13}{y + 2} = 27\), \(\dfrac{13}{2x + 1} + \dfrac{7}{y + 2} = 33\).
solution: Substitute \(m = \dfrac{1}{2x + 1}\) and \(n = \dfrac{1}{y + 2}\): \(7m + 13n = 27\) ...(3) and \(13m + 7n = 33\) ...(4). Adding: \(20m + 20n = 60\Rightarrow m + n = 3\). Subtracting (3) from (4): \(6m - 6n = 6\Rightarrow m - n = 1\). So \(m = 2\), \(n = 1\). Then \(\dfrac{1}{2x + 1} = 2 \Rightarrow 4x + 2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{1}{4}\); and \(\dfrac{1}{y + 2} = 1 \Rightarrow y + 2 = 1 \Rightarrow y = -1\).

stem: In a certain race, there are three boys A, B, C. The winning probability of A is twice than B and the winning probability of B is twice than C. If \(P(A) + P(B) + P(C) = 1\), then find the probability of win for each boy.
solution: Given \(P(A) = 2P(B)\) and \(P(B) = 2P(C)\), so \(P(A) = 4P(C)\). Then \(4P(C) + 2P(C) + P(C) = 1 \Rightarrow 7P(C) = 1\). Hence \(P(C) = \dfrac{1}{7}\), \(P(B) = \dfrac{2}{7}\) and \(P(A) = \dfrac{4}{7}\).

stem: The divisor and quotient of the number \(6123\) are same and the remainder is half the divisor. Find the divisor.
solution: Let divisor \(=\) quotient \(= d\); then remainder \(= \dfrac{d}{2}\). Since dividend \(=\) divisor \(\times\) quotient \(+\) remainder: \(6123 = d^2 + \dfrac{d}{2}\), i.e. \(12246 = 2d^2 + d\), so \(2d^2 + d - 12246 = 0\). Using the formula, \(d = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4(2)(-12246)}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{97969}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm 313}{4}\), giving \(d = 78\) or \(d = -78.5\). Ignoring the negative value, the divisor is \(78\).

A three digit number is equal to \(17\) times the sum of its digits. If \(198\) is added to the number, the digits are interchanged. The addition of first and third digit is \(1\) less than middle digit. Find the number.
solution: Let the number be \(100x + 10y + z\). Then \(100x + 10y + z = 17(x + y + z) \Rightarrow 83x - 7y - 16z = 0\) ...(1). Adding \(198\) reverses the digits: \((100x + 10y + z) + 198 = 100z + 10y + x \Rightarrow 99z - 99x = 198 \Rightarrow z = x + 2\) ...(2). Also \(x + z = y - 1\), so \(x + (x + 2) = y - 1 \Rightarrow y = 2x + 3\). Substituting in (1): \(83x - 7(2x + 3) - 16(x + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow 53x - 53 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1\), \(y = 5\), \(z = 3\). Thus the number is \(153\).
